items.text: Answer: Pick the diploma whose work needs your hands, your presence or your judgment, and which a named employer or scheme is paying for.
Run any diploma through these four tests before you pay, and ask for the approval in writing.
Ask Is this diploma approved by the body that matters for the job it leads to?
Good sign An engineering diploma from a college on the AICTE approved list, or a health diploma that leads to a named council registration.

blocks.heading: Six Diploma Families, Strongest Growth First

items.text: Two questions decide a family: will the work still exist, and can your income grow past a fixed pay ladder.
Why this rating Work can be sold to clients in any city and later become a product.
Why it holds Data and AI roles are among the fastest-growing in India.
Run the four questions first, then pass the three proofs: the questions test whether this diploma suits you, and the proofs show you can earn from it.
Site work means heat and early starts, lab work means precision and shifts, and a machine shop means noise and safety rules.
Count the fee, travel, hostel and the earnings you give up.

blocks.heading: Branches or Colleges Are the Weak Ones
rows: In 2024-25 India had 3,566 polytechnics, 59% of them private. About 33% of 9.7 lakh approved seats sat empty in 2022-23, down from 48% in 2017-18.
Which branches or colleges are the weak ones.
The 2026 regulations require 57 allied and healthcare professions to register, for five years at a time.
Registration has not started, and it does not say which diplomas will qualify.
Cabinet approval of PM Surya Ghar (February 2024) and All India Radio News (23 September 2026)

PM Surya Ghar aims at rooftop solar for 1 crore households. By 23 September 2026 it had reached over 51 lakh families, with 14.8 GW commissioned, and the government says it is creating local work for solar technicians.
It gives no count of jobs filled, and it does not say how many of them suit diploma holders.
WEF Future of Jobs 2025, as reported by The Week

India's fastest-growing roles are big data, AI and machine learning, and security management specialists. 30% of companies in India plan skills-based hiring by dropping degree requirements, against 19% worldwide.
Those top roles mostly ask for more than a three-year diploma.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Pay in India: AmbitionBox shows diploma trainee engineers earning Rs 1.3 to 3.3 lakh a year in their first three years, with an average starting pay near Rs 1.3 lakh, based on about 19,700 salaries (page updated March 2025, checked on 16 November 2026). A government Junior Engineer post sits at Level 6 of the 7th pay matrix, with basic pay of Rs 35,400 to Rs 1,12,400 a month ( AglaSem, checked on 17 November 2026). Pay varies by city, employer and skill, so check current postings.
